name: countersign-agent-api
description:
Countersign sits between an autonomous AI agent and payment execution. An agent submits a **payment
intent**; Countersign authenticates the agent, evaluates the request against its immutable spending
policy with a deterministic engine, and returns one of three decisions:

| Decision | HTTP status | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `AUTHORIZED` | `201` | Allowed. The PayPal Payouts request is submitted. |
| `PENDING_APPROVAL` | `201` | Within limits but needs a human countersign (threshold or new recipient). Budget is reserved. |
| `DENIED` | `422` | Hard policy violation. Recorded, never sent to PayPal. |

The agent can never approve its own payment. Approvals are made by a human in the Countersign console.
Payout settlement is confirmed asynchronously (PayPal webhooks plus reconciliation polling), so poll
`GET /agent/payment-intents/{id}` for the final status.

**Authentication.** Every agent request carries the agent's bearer token (`cs_<agentId>_<secret>`),
issued once when the agent is registered. The token determines which agent (and therefore which
policy) applies; any `agent_id` in a request body is ignored.

**Idempotency.** Send an `Idempotency-Key` header on every `POST`. Re-sending the same key with the same
body returns the original intent (`200` with `Idempotent-Replay: true`). Re-using a key with a
different body is rejected with `409 IDEMPOTENCY_KEY_REUSED`.

**Amounts** are decimal strings in major units (for example `"49.00"`). Currency is an ISO code; the
sandbox policy allows `USD`.

This is a PayPal **Sandbox** prototype. No real money moves.
